findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple area in need of physical repair:
1) The caulking around the mop sink is beginning to darken and fragment.
2) The wall to the left of the dish machine has an accumulation of debris.
Discussed with the person in charge. Replace caulking at the mop sink and clean the wall next to the dish machine.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of soil debris on multiple soda nozzles at the server station. CORRECTED- all nozzles were removed to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed bacon cooked yesterday in walk in cooler was not date marked. CORRECTED- PIC placed label on cooked bacon. Ensure that all temperature controlled ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours are date marked to indicate the 7 day maximum holding time. [Pf]
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed accumulation of dust on multiple kitchen ceiling vents. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. Ensure that ceiling vents are clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection. [C]
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Daylight is visible along the bottom edge of the back door. Weather stripping is missing from that area. Replace the weather stripping on the back door so it is tight-fitting and daylight is not visible along the edges.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(C) Outer Openings, Protected. (C) Exterior doors used as exits need not be self-closing if they are: (1) Solid and tight-fitting. [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
PIC present at the beginning of this inspection has not completed ANSI-approved allergen awareness training. CORRECTED- A CFM with allergen training arrived near the end of this inspection. Ensure a CFM with allergen training is present during all shifts of food prep and service.
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Knife on the cookline observed stored in between the prep cooler and the counter. CORRECTED- Knife was removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Knife will be stored on a clean surface between uses.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. [C]
